claims.text: A page's JavaScript runs on a single main thread; the event loop takes one task at a time from a queue (user input, timers, network completions) and runs it to completion before the next.
claims.source_hint: HTML spec: event loops (task queues, run to completion); MDN: The event loop / JavaScript execution model

claims.text: The browser updates the rendering between tasks, so a long-running task delays both handling of other input and redrawing the page.
claims.source_hint: HTML spec: event loop processing model (update the rendering step after a task)

claims.text: Network requests started by page JavaScript (fetch/XMLHttpRequest) are carried out by the browser without blocking the page's main thread; the response is handled later by a queued task.
claims.source_hint: MDN: Using the Fetch API; HTML spec networking task source

claims.text: The browser does some of its own work, such as waiting for the network, outside the page's JavaScript thread, but a page's JavaScript handlers run one at a time on that thread.
claims.source_hint: MDN: JavaScript execution model (agents, single thread per agent)

claims.text: The www/ pages at stage-0 contain no JavaScript.
DonHang.App loads the product list from GET /api/v1/products with package:http, awaiting the response.

Running `const end = Date.now() + 5000; while (Date.now() < end) {}` in the DevTools console blocks the page's main thread for about five seconds: the page does not respond to selection or clicks until it ends.
claims.source_hint: Chrome DevTools console evaluates in the page's main thread; HTML spec event loop

claims.text: Short tasks keep a page quick to react; one long task blocks everything behind it.

DonHang.App is a Flutter web build running in the browser on the page's main thread; package:http uses the browser client on the web, so the request is handed to the browser; heavy Dart work on the web runs on the main thread and would freeze the page.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: scripts/up.sh (flutter build web); pub.dev http (BrowserClient on web); refs/flutter-website perf/isolates.md (no isolates on web)

claims.text: Code typed in the DevTools Console runs on the page's main thread; a click made while it is busy is queued and handled after it finishes (the link then opens).
claims.source_hint: reviewer r1 headless Chrome run (link opened ~18 ms after the loop)
